                    ### Question
                    What is the treatment of choice for a 38-year-old man diagnosed with Cushing's disease in relation to a pituitary macroadenoma 22 mm in diameter?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Initially try medical treatment and, if it is not effective, resort to surgery.
opb. Adrenalectomy
opc. Selective surgical resection of the adenoma.
opd. Radiation therapy to try to decrease the tumor size.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Cushing's disease, particularly when associated with a pituitary macroadenoma, is primarily treated through surgical intervention. For a 38-year-old man with a 22 mm pituitary macroadenoma, selective surgical resection of the adenoma is considered the treatment of choice, as it directly addresses the source of excess cortisol production. While initial medical treatment may be attempted in some cases, it is not the preferred first-line approach for macroadenomas of this size. Radiation therapy is typically reserved for cases where surgery is not feasible or in cases of residual disease post-surgery. Therefore, the most effective and consensus-supported option is selective surgical resection of the adenoma.
